title: Neglected tropical disease therapeutics
bottleneck: Diseases like Chagas, leishmaniasis, and sleeping sickness afflict over a billion people but attract minimal R&D because patients cannot pay; treatments are often decades old, toxic, and difficult to administer.
why_it_blocks: Market-driven drug development systematically ignores diseases of poverty, leaving ancient, toxic regimens as the standard of care.
current_state: Product-development partnerships have delivered a handful of improved treatments, but the pipeline remains thin and dependent on philanthropy, the same fragility WHO documents in the antibacterial ecosystem. The market failure is structural: developing drugs for patients who cannot pay requires sustained philanthropic or public funding. Product-development partnerships have shown the model can work, delivering improved treatments for sleeping sickness and visceral leishmaniasis, but the portfolio remains far too small for the burden.

sources.title: World Health Organization Warns That Antibiotic Innovation Still Insufficient
